# Migration baselines

The six resource manifests capture the TypeScript program from commit d847692,
with AWS 7.44.0, Cloudflare 6.20.0, Random 4.21.1 and Pulumi 3.261.0 mocked SDKs.
They contain synthetic identifiers and secrets only. Scenarios cover foundation,
legacy, transition (both hosts and fleet), rolling-only mode, apex certificate creation, and the settled cutover with an external certificate. All deployed
resource types, logical names and input values are compared with the Go program.
JSON policy object ordering and secret-envelope representation are normalized;
array order and generated user data are compared exactly.

`legacy.sh`, `rolling.sh`, and `cutover.sh` are exact output bytes from the original TypeScript
bootstrap function, including its JSON property order. They are test fixtures,
not scripts to execute on hosts. Go tests parse their shell/Python programs and
compare generated bytes so a language-only change cannot trigger a host refresh.

Keep these baselines fixed for the migration. Future intentional infrastructure
changes should update corresponding expectations with a reviewed explanation.

To regenerate, export `infra/index.ts`, `rolling.ts`, `userdata.ts`,
`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `tsconfig.json` from the recorded
TypeScript commit into a temporary directory. Install its pinned npm packages,
copy `capture.ts` into that directory, and run `npx tsx capture.ts MODE OUTPUT`
for each of `foundation legacy transition rolling cutover apex`. The generator
uses Pulumi mocks only and synthetic identifiers. Inspect the resulting fixture
diff against the source change before replacing any baseline.
